arguments.claim: Si is tetravalent like C; forms chains, rings, chiral centres
Si is ~100-1400x more abundant than C in rocky-planet crust (source-dependent)
Hypervalent (5/6-coordinate) Si gives extra reaction pathways
Long polysilanes (~500 Si-Si) and silicones exist
Directed evolution produced enzymes forming Si–C bonds; biology can learn Si chemistry
Concentrated sulfuric acid supports more organosilicon diversity than water
Cold aprotic solvents (liquid N2/CH4) keep most Si chemistry intact
Silicate clay crystals may have been the first genetic material
Si–Si (222) much weaker than C–C (346) while Si–O (452) is stronger; oxygen sinks Si
Nearly all Si–X bonds hydrolyse in water; Si only a rare heteroatom in aqueous life
SiO2 is an insoluble polymeric solid; no CO2-like gaseous waste or cycle
Few stable Si=Si/Si=O/Si=C pi bonds; much less structural diversity
Silanes are thermodynamically uphill from silica (SiH4 ΔG +434 vs CH4 −142 kJ/mol)
C ~10x more abundant than Si cosmically
Cryosolvents dissolve almost nothing (>ppm for only ~a dozen small molecules)
Lava/silicate-melt worlds break Si–O bonds on ms timescales; no stable information
No natural enzyme makes Si–C or breaks Si–O despite Si abundance on Earth
Overall: Si-based life implausible in all assessed solvents (Si as heteroatom possible)
